author: Gamblor3809
body:
Top tier amities you wanna get are- +40% crit, +20% block chance (parapet), +5 ward turns, +50% positive status, +5% recover of max hp per turn, +5% ward recovery per turn, +7% pet blocking, +25% accessory bonus, +100% memory rewards, +5% view distance

A good reference is ornalegends.com/amities.html

author: KevineCove
body:
These are the bonuses that I consider relevant. Most of these are hard to fully take advantage of as a new player, however.

These are things that are pretty much immediately helpful for any player:

* You will recover 5% of your maximum mana per turn
   * Often with this you never have to waste turns taking potions; you can stay on the offensive all the time. Obviously useful for magic-based classes but many melee builds have good skills that consume mana as well.
* Skills that grand ward absorption will grant 5% more absorption
   * Solid amity that only gets better with time. Going from 50% to 55% absorption isn't necessarily a huge boost, but an ability that grants 85% absorption will go up to 90% and this effectively reduces the HP damage you take by 1/3. That said, regardless of tier if you find yourself still having ward when you die, this demonstrably improves survivability.
* Positive status effects will last 50% longer
   * Most useful for making Deific Channel last longer, but this isn't relevant until T8. That said, there are still (less useful) temporary buffs that appear earlier in the game that you can take advantage of with this amity.
* You will gain 5% additional view distance
   * Situationally helpful for all the obvious reasons
* You are more likely to encounter monsters for quests
   * Situationally helpful for all the obvious reasons.
* You will receive 100% additional rewards when completing memories
   * Memory hunts are rewarding enough on their own, but doubling (or tripling, as Oracle) the yield of a memory hunt, especially if you find a couchable amity, is basically a free orn farm.
* Accessory effectiveness increased by 25%
   * The most infamous use is to stack with Band of Gods while farming endless, but for an early game player you can use this for accessories that boost stats or throw them on your Monster Tomes for more experience gain. If you're getting experience from any source other than raiding, this should be your go-to.
* Simple attacks will deal 40% more damage
   * I don't know a ton about this amity other than that I know it's popular among Realmshifters. I suspect it may be useful in lower tiers depending on the class.
* You will encounter 70% more monsters
   * Situationally helpful for all the obvious reasons. This is particularly useful during Riftbreaks.

These amities are great in endgame but are difficult to get the best use out of:

* Critical damage increased by 40%
   * In early game, it's difficult to get a good crit build, and lower tier gear is the kind of stuff you don't want to waste money putting your expensive adornments on anyway. At T10 you can start creating 100% crit builds which make this insanely powerful.
* Increases X damage by 30%
   * Mostly used for Ultima raiding builds; getting a legendary that stacks a couple of these will stack the damage boost and lead to some truly ridiculous damage. Before T10 you can really only boost one element (ideally your faction element) or use Omnimancy at T9, neither of which are anywhere near as useful as Ultima.
* You will begin battle with 5 ward turns activated
   * Mostly useful in PvP and in towers where some enemies have enough foresight to go first (especially useful when playing Summoner)
* You will recover 5% ward each turn
   * Not very useful until you get get a decent amount of ward absorption; otherwise you'll still lose all of your HP even if you have tons of ward. Becomes relevant in T8 when you unlock Divine Bastion.
* There is a 20% chance to be protected from attacks that would deal 100% of your maximum HP
   * Most useful for PvP, especially if you have a Legendary/Ornate amity where this is stacked with another effect. For most other game content you aren't going to encounter hits that deal this much damage. Raids are an exception to this but there are better bonuses to have for raiding than one that's purely defensive.
* Your summons will be 30% stronger
   * Amazing once you can actually start summoning monsters of interest. At T8 when Buggane becomes available it will be the best amity until you reach endgame.

author: dfoley323
body:
Just a few additional tips:

* monuments guild / fishing guild are the best way to get additional mnemonics
* you can also get some from towers (t9+) 
* plan to get 2 of every good amity you find.  You might not need them now, but it might be a year until you can get them again.
* Even if you dont plan on using it right now,if an A+ amity is found (orna legends), i would get 2x of them if possible incase you need it in the future
* amities repeat yearly, assuming there are no new amities added.  Meaning there are parties (orna legends) that hunt t10 amities and have years worth of data.   I highly recommend joining orna legends discord at t10 and reading all the rules/mechanics.  I waited a long time to start hunting and regret it.   It is not complicated at all once you get the hand of it, and good amities 100% change your play style/builds.  

EG

I have 2x   40% crit dmg/15% dmg at full hp.   Now when i play BeoH, i can run swansong, and do 200-300k a turn in horde dungeons.  Others might just have the 2x40% crit dmg and while still nice will be doing considerably less dmg than me.  

Another good example, is an ultra rare amity with 30% dragon dmg / 30% arcane dmg....This is amazing for ultima/towerfall, Top teir, you will be doing more dmg than everyone else with it, but it was only found 1x in the last 2 years, so being part of the communities pays off.
